prompt:
Build RoomSync, a usable local-first collaboration service for small JSON documents, in contrib/roomsync in this real ws repository. It is for an offline workspace dashboard whose browser clients can disconnect, queue edits, reconnect, see conflicts, and recover their documents after the server crashes. Preserve the ws public API, package metadata, production files and all original tests. Use the repository's actual ws implementation for the server transport. Deliver a standalone locally installable RoomSync package with CommonJS and ESM entry points, public TypeScript declarations, a Node/browser client, an offline web interface, a CLI, maintained tests, protocol/operations documentation and an offline example. Node 22 or newer is acceptable for RoomSync. Use only ws and Node standard libraries as runtime dependencies; development tools are unrestricted. Publish the ESM wrapper at index.mjs and include a README.md and maintained tests under test/. Do not publish or commit.

Implement the following public contract from contrib/roomsync/index.js (CommonJS), with matching named ESM exports. All asynchronous methods return promises. Errors have a nonempty message and the exact code described below. Do not expose filesystem paths, stack traces or configured tokens in network errors.

openStore(directory, options?) returns a persistent store. Options maxDocumentBytes (default 1048576) and maxTransactionBytes (default 4194304) are positive safe integers; reject invalid or unknown options with INVALID. Only one live store may own a directory, including across processes: a competing open rejects LOCKED, a clean close releases it, and a killed owner's store can be reopened without manual lock deletion. Reject a symlink directory, symlink room storage, or traversal outside the directory. openStore eagerly validates all existing rooms and rejects CORRUPT without overwriting corrupt persisted data.

Room names match /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$/. Document keys are nonempty strings up to 256 UTF-16 units, with NUL rejected; __proto__, constructor, prototype and Unicode keys are ordinary safe keys. Values must be finite JSON data: reject undefined, NaN/infinities, bigint, functions, symbols, sparse arrays, cycles and objects with non-plain prototypes. Never mutate supplied data or expose mutable references into store state. Byte limits count UTF-8 bytes of JSON.stringify(value) for each resulting document and JSON.stringify(transaction) for the transaction. Validate the complete transaction before writing.

store.snapshot(room) returns {room, revision, minimumRevision, documents}, with documents an array of {key,value} sorted by JavaScript string sort order. A new room reads as revision 0, minimumRevision 0, documents []. store.transact(room, transaction, options?) accepts {clientId, requestId, expectedRevision, operations}. clientId/requestId are nonempty strings up to 128 characters without NUL; expectedRevision is a nonnegative safe integer; operations is a nonempty array. The optional third argument accepts only signal. An already-aborted signal rejects with its exact reason and no effects. A successful nonempty transaction increments that room's revision exactly once and returns {room,revision,clientId,requestId,duplicate:false}. expectedRevision must equal the current revision or reject CONFLICT with currentRevision. Concurrent transactions are serialized without lost writes.

Operations are {op:'put',key,value}, {op:'delete',key}, and {op:'patch',key,patch}. Delete and patch require an existing document or reject NOT_FOUND. patch is a nonempty array implementing RFC 6902 add/remove/replace/move/copy/test using RFC 6901 pointer decoding. Support root add/replace/test and copying the root; reject root remove with INVALID (delete the document with the outer delete operation). Support arrays, the add '-' token, the empty root pointer, escaped slash/tilde, deep structural test equality and safe special property names. Reject malformed pointers, invalid array indices, missing parents, moves into descendants, invalid operation shapes and unknown fields with INVALID; failed test rejects CONFLICT. A failure anywhere rolls back the entire transaction, including earlier operations on other documents; it changes no revision, journal, subscriber event or deduplication state.

Deduplicate by (room,clientId,requestId) before checking the current expectedRevision: the same semantic transaction (object property order is irrelevant) returns the original receipt with duplicate:true, without another write/event/revision, even after restart or compaction. Reuse with a different payload rejects ID_REUSE. Failed transactions do not reserve their request IDs. Keep room state independent. store.subscribe(room, listener) synchronously returns an unsubscribe function; after durable commit notify each current listener once, in revision order, with an isolated {room,revision,clientId,requestId,operations} event. Listener failures must not change commit outcomes or prevent other listeners from receiving events.

store.history(room,{after,limit}?) returns events in increasing revision order strictly after after (default 0), with positive integer limit (default 1000, maximum 10000). after must be a nonnegative safe integer no greater than the room's current revision. store.compact(room,{through}) atomically checkpoints through a valid revision between minimumRevision and revision; it can retain newer history. minimumRevision becomes through, history with after below it rejects HISTORY_GONE and includes minimumRevision/currentRevision; after equal to it works. Current documents, pending newer events and all successful idempotency receipts survive restart and compaction.

Use an append-only journal at directory/rooms/<room>/events.ndjson. Each terminated line is a JSON envelope {payload,sha256}, where sha256 is the lowercase SHA-256 of UTF-8 JSON.stringify(payload). Acknowledgement occurs only after the journal record has been flushed to stable storage. On recovery, discard only an unterminated final line, validate every terminated line and checksum, and reject CORRUPT for malformed/checksum-invalid complete records or inconsistent history. Snapshot and compaction publication must be crash-safe; a process killed during a write or compaction must reopen with a consistent prefix and every acknowledged commit exactly once. Directory durability, temporary file cleanup and orphaned lock recovery must be documented and actually tested with child processes and SIGKILL. Do not replace these tests with a timer or a mocked process.

store.exportRoom(room) returns a deterministic Buffer archive of that room, including current documents, revision, compaction floor, retained history and idempotency data, with integrity protection. store.importRoom(targetRoom, bytes) validates the full archive before creating the target room; only an empty/nonexistent target is allowed, otherwise CONFLICT. The target name may differ from the exported room; all returned room fields must use the target. Corrupt input rejects CORRUPT without changing any room. Export/import must preserve Unicode, null/scalar/array documents, safe keys, deduplication and history behavior. store.close() is idempotent, settles accepted work and closes file/lock resources; operations started after closing reject CLOSED.

createServer({store,host?,port?,tokens,allowedOrigins?,maxPendingBytes?}) starts HTTP and WebSocket service and returns {url,close}. Default host is 127.0.0.1 and port is 0. tokens is an object with distinct nonempty read, write and admin token strings. All APIs require Bearer authentication, with read < write < admin privileges; errors are JSON {error:{code,message,...}} using 400 INVALID/CORRUPT, 401 AUTH, 403 PERMISSION, 404 NOT_FOUND, 409 CONFLICT/ID_REUSE, 410 HISTORY_GONE and 413 LIMIT. Successful API GET and POST requests return HTTP 200. No token in query strings, logs, HTML or health replies. GET /health is public and returns {ok:true}. API routes: GET /api/rooms/:room -> snapshot; POST /api/rooms/:room/transactions -> transaction receipt (write); GET /api/rooms/:room/events?after=N&limit=N -> {events}; POST /api/rooms/:room/compact with {through} (admin); GET /api/rooms/:room/archive -> bytes (read); POST /api/rooms/:room/archive with bytes -> imported snapshot (admin). Bound request bodies and reject malformed encodings, paths, JSON and query parameters without partial writes. Server close disconnects clients and releases sockets, but leaves caller-owned store open.

WebSocket endpoint /sync uses JSON text messages. First message is {type:'hello',token,room,after}; authenticate before returning data. Within a bounded timeout reject unauthenticated connections. The first successful response is {type:'welcome',snapshot,events,reset}, taking a consistent snapshot and retained events since after. If after is below the compaction floor, set reset:true and events:[]; otherwise reset:false. Subsequent committed transactions produce {type:'event',event}. A racing commit appears either in welcome or as one subsequent live event, never omitted or duplicated. The writer sends {type:'transaction',id,transaction}; respond {type:'ack',id,receipt} or {type:'error',id,code,message,currentRevision?}. Read-only clients cannot write. Unrecognized types and malformed frames must not commit or crash the process. Reject binary frames and bound message sizes. If an Origin is present, accept only a configured allowedOrigin or the server's own origin. The maximum incoming WebSocket JSON text frame is 4194304 UTF-8 bytes. Bound per-client outgoing bytes using maxPendingBytes (positive integer; default 1048576), disconnect slow consumers without stalling durable writers, and clear timers/listeners on all close/error paths.

Export RoomClient from the Node entry and a browser-safe ESM entry browser.mjs. new RoomClient({url,token,room,clientId,WebSocket?,storage?,onChange?}) creates an initially offline client; url is the HTTP server origin, WebSocket is an injectable compatible WebSocket constructor, and optional storage is a synchronous Web Storage-like getItem/setItem/removeItem adapter. connect() resolves after a valid welcome; close() stops automatic reconnect, rejects unsettled submit promises with CLOSED, and retains persisted pending records for a future client instance. snapshot() returns an isolated last synchronized snapshot; pending() returns isolated {requestId,transaction,status} records, with status 'pending' or 'conflict'. submit(operations,{requestId?,expectedRevision?}?) queues an edit and resolves with its durable receipt. Default expectedRevision is the local synchronized revision plus earlier pending edits; generate a unique requestId if absent. Retain queued requests and current snapshot in storage, namespaced by origin/room/clientId, without persisting the token. Reconnect with bounded exponential backoff and replay unchanged IDs in order so a lost ack cannot duplicate a write. Conflicts remain visible as status:'conflict' in pending(), stop dependent replay, and require resolve(requestId,{action:'discard'}) or resolve(requestId,{action:'retry',expectedRevision}) before proceeding. Retry gets a fresh request ID and replays that transaction with the explicitly supplied revision. resolve returns a promise once the local queue update is persisted; completion of replay is visible in pending() and snapshot(). Unknown request IDs or invalid resolution options reject INVALID. Expose transport errors and conflicts through onChange and the affected submit promise; never silently overwrite other clients' edits. Guard corrupted persisted client state, simultaneous close/reconnect, out-of-order or duplicate frames, and late events from old sockets. Browser entry must run with no Node globals or dynamic code generation.

Serve a usable offline UI at /. It must let a person supply a token, select a room, view documents and revision, create/edit/delete a JSON document, see connection status, see pending/conflicting edits and explicitly discard/retry a conflict, export/import a room archive where permitted, and reconnect after a server restart. Render room/document data as text, including HTML-like document keys and contents. For keyboard and automation access, expose exact accessible field labels 'Token', 'Room', 'Document key', 'JSON value' and button names 'Connect', 'Save document', 'Delete document'; label the remaining actions descriptively. Use the delivered client implementation, local static assets and accessible labels; no external CDN, analytics or remote service. Obtain real browser interaction evidence of two clients editing, an actual conflict, offline queue/reconnect, and safe text rendering.

The CLI is bin/roomsync.js. Support --help and serve --directory DIR --tokens-file FILE [--host HOST] [--port PORT]; token file contains the same read/write/admin object. Print one JSON ready line {url} on stdout, keep diagnostics on stderr, and gracefully drain on SIGINT/SIGTERM, exiting with code 0 after a clean shutdown. Document library, HTTP, WebSocket and offline-client contracts; include operational recovery/backup procedures and a runnable offline example at examples/offline-demo.js. Add maintained tests for state isolation, transaction atomicity, all patch operations, idempotency, concurrent clients, corruption recovery, real SIGKILL/restart, compaction, archive integrity, auth roles, replay/live handoff, reconnect/lost ack, safe rendering and resource cleanup. Run the original ws suite, new tests, lint/type validation, the example, real browser scenarios and packaging checks. Install the packed ws and RoomSync tarballs into an exclusive temporary consumer outside the checkout and verify CJS, ESM, client and CLI use; this must work without a link back to the source checkout. Do not modify the original ws package just to include the companion product. Continue until implementation, validation, documentation and delivery are finished; report exact successful checks and any gaps. The frozen root node_modules includes TypeScript, @types/node, @types/ws and @playwright/test for validation. Use these installed tools; browser installation is independent of the VelarOS account.
